title: Site brief
summary: A one-page site built from a written brief: exact copy, the requested sections and link, nothing invented, and the delivered page matches what the seller declared.

criteria.label: Every required copy string from the brief appears in the visible text
A link with the requested button text points to the requested address
Each requested section has its own heading or section id
No guarantee, price, certification or verification claim that the brief does not contain
Page background matches the requested dark or light style, read from its CSS
The delivered page hashes to the sha256 the seller declared, and that value is well formed
The page does what the brief asked, section by section

anchors.1: Most of the brief is ignored: sections, copy or purpose are missing or replaced by the seller's own content.
anchors.3: The main sections and purpose follow the brief. One or two requested elements are weak, misplaced or only partly there.
anchors.5: Every requested section, line of copy and action is present where the brief puts it, and the page reads as the product page the brief describes.

examples.1: The brief asks for four sections and a tagline. The page has a different tagline and two sections the buyer never mentioned.
examples.3: All four sections exist, but the closing section only repeats the intro and the requested button sits below the fold behind other links.
examples.5: The four sections appear in the requested order with the requested lines, and the button directly follows the intro.

criteria.label: Nothing is invented: no facts, numbers, names or promises beyond the brief

anchors.1: Several statements the brief does not support: invented numbers, customers, features, guarantees or credentials.
anchors.3: Mostly the brief's own content. Filler sentences or mild embellishment appear, but none promises something checkable that is false.
anchors.5: Every sentence traces to the brief or is neutral structure such as a section label. Nothing added that a reader could take as a fact.

examples.1: A footer line says the company is award-winning and a badge claims a 100% success rate. The brief says neither.
examples.3: Step descriptions add a sentence about what happens next that the brief does not state, but it makes no claim that can be wrong.
examples.5: Beyond the brief's copy the page has only headings and generic navigation labels.

criteria.label: Polish judged from the page text and structure only: no screenshots are used

anchors.1: The text reads as broken or unfinished: placeholders, repeated blocks, stray template text or unreadable structure.
anchors.3: Complete and readable. Some awkward wording, inconsistent labels or leftover scaffolding.
anchors.5: Clean, consistent wording and a clear order from the top heading to the footer, with no leftover scaffolding.

examples.1: Template instructions such as 'replace this text' remain in the visible copy.
examples.3: Button labels differ between sections for the same action.
examples.5: Headings, labels and actions use one voice and one naming throughout.

criteria.label: The buyer states whether the work was accepted
